newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ELECTROLUX HUNGARY INJECTION HELPS SAAB FIGHTER BID.
newsitem.headline: ELECTROLUX HUNGARY INJECTION HELPS SAAB FIGHTER BID.

text.p: Electrolux said on Friday a $33 million equity raise for its Hungarian refrigerator unit will be 100 percent offset against sister company Saab's bid to sell JAS 39 Gripen fighter aircraft to Hungary.
Electrolux, which, like Saab is part of Sweden's Wallenberg industrial sphere, announced its decision to raise the registered capital of Electrolux-Lehel by six billion forints on Friday.
"This goes 100 percent to the offset deal as it is an investment which comes right out of share capital," Electrolux Hungary's president Tibor Kertesz, told Reuters.
Saab is competing with a number of aircraft makers to replace Hungary's fleet of 30 Soviet MiG-21s and MiG-23s which will be obsolete by the end of the century.

Also in the race for the $1 billion contract are Lockheed Martin's F16, McDonnell Douglas/Northrop's F-18 and Dassault's Mirage 2000-5, while Russia's state arms agency Rosvooruzhenie is also reported to be considering offering Su-27s, Su-30s and Su-39s.

The fighter procurement tender had been due for publication last summer but Hungary postponed the decision until after a decision by NATO on expansion, expected at the alliance's summit in Madrid next month.

The Wallenberg group was the first to sign an industrial offset deal with the Hungarian government in September 1995 and Friday's announcement takes its direct investment in Hungary usable as offset to around $100 million, far ahead of any of its rivals, who only signed industrial packages this year.
Kertesz said the new investment will finance developments at the company's new $15 million chest freezer plant at the central Hungarian town of Jaszbereny which opened on March.
Kertesz said the investment will boost the company's exports out of Hungary and create around 300 new jobs
"Electrolux has the target of maintaining the same market share in Central Europe as in Western Europe of at least a 25 percent," Kertesz said.
He added that Electrolux-Lehel expected its share in Hungary's industrial exports to rise to eight percent from between four and five percent as a result of the capital increase.
Kertesz said the company saw turnover totalling 47 billion forints ($260.03 million) in 1996 and produced 1.1 million refrigerators in Hungary.
